# Universe24

> One integer rule on a cubic lattice, read through clicks: the formulas it shares with nature and adds. A paper archived on Zenodo and at the tag v1.1.0, its supplement with every proof, the law of the lattice, the derivations as scripts, the engine V2 with its tests and the paper's engine at the tag v1.1.0, and the two slits' universe. Author: Alon Gonen, independent researcher, Haifa, Israel (ORCID 0009-0008-2701-4599). Licence MIT. Permanent record: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23190113

## In plain words

Suppose nature is discrete: space is made of Nodes, and between one Node and the next nothing moves faster than light. A cubic centimetre then holds an astronomical number of Nodes, so no centre can know and decide for all of them; each Node acts on its own, by a rule of its own, seeing only itself and its six neighbours. Universe24 is that rule: one line of integer arithmetic with no free parameter. A Node holds its level now, its level one interval before, and a remainder; at every interval it takes its six neighbours' levels with weights, adds its own level with a weight, subtracts its level of the interval before, adds the carried remainder, and divides by a fixed integer, keeping the new remainder. Nothing is lost, so the rule is exactly reversible. The weights come from the family's pair of integers and the Node's paces; at the vacuum's paces the rule is a discrete wave equation, and from it the paper derives formulas that nature shows and adds formulas of its own with blind predictions. A world is read only through clicks of declared counting regions. The paper's one claim: the rule helps compute things in nature. Every number in the paper is reproduced by a script in the repository.

## Read first

- [The paper, 40 pages](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/papers/one_rule/Universe24_Paper.pdf): "Universe24: one simple rule, the formulas it shares with nature and adds" (Alon Gonen, 2026)
- [The supplement, Online Resource 1, 85 pages](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/papers/one_rule/Universe24_Supplement.pdf): the claims list and the algebraic steps of every derivation
- [The time paper, 21 pages](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/papers/spacetime_events/arrow.pdf): "A discrete spacetime of events in whole numbers: why clocks slow, why nothing outruns light, and why time has a direction only where something was measured" (Alon Gonen, 2026), its source, run and checks in papers/spacetime_events/, built and run by its build.sh
- [README](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/README.md): the aim, the plain words, what the repository holds, how to run a world, what is open

## The documents

- [The law of the lattice](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/docs/ALGEBRA.md): one algebraic line per rule, the families, the bodies, the clicks, every experiment's formula and blind expectation
- [The decisions in force](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/docs/HIGHLIGHTS.md): one line each
- [The engine](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/docs/ENGINE.md): the words, the main loop and Rule3, the files, the output, the gates, how to run a world, the known issues and the open items
- [Contributing](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/CONTRIBUTING.md): forks and pull requests, the ground rules, the checks
- [What changed](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/CHANGELOG.md): one entry per version, 2.0.0 the engine V2 against 1.1.0, the paper's engine

## The code

- [Repository on GitHub](https://github.com/Closer24/Universe24): the derivations as scripts (tools/derivations/), the implementation (src/event_universe/), the tests, the two slits' universe (examples/events/two_slits/)
- [Zenodo record](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23190113): the archived version 1.1.0 with a DOI, the one to cite
